new: Calibrating a room works again: since v218 the second cross made both crosses and their line vanish and the headset stayed not lined up. The cause is taken to be one of v218's savings (it is the only one in that path, and v217 works on the owner's headset); it could not be reproduced without a headset.
The studio's file is about a third smaller: its comments are left out, and the parts for converting models and for the page's arrows come only when they are needed.

Real-world occlusion and the spaceships now load when a headset session starts, or earlier on a device that can enter VR, or when someone in your room flies a ship; otherwise a phone or a laptop no longer fetches them.
A page that has run a while never takes these files from a newer release: it waits to be reloaded.
The developer notebook loads only once developer mode is on; a note left unsent while it is off goes once it is on again.
The headset's panels, Stories cards, menu and subtitles are made only once they are first drawn: on a laptop a story no longer makes about 27 of them (up to 50 MB had they been drawn).
test: In a headset in a fresh room: Calibrate, place the two crosses; both and the line between them should stay and the room say it is lined up. If not, note the notice and the menu's line-up text right after the second trigger pull.
Open the studio, upload an FBX or OBJ model and convert it: it works as before.
In the studio's edit mode, select an item: the arrows still move and size it.
Turn developer mode on: the notebook's round button appears at the bottom right.
Open a story on a laptop and on a phone: it looks and plays as before.
untested: Everything in a headset: nothing since v220 has been tried in one.
In a headset: real-world occlusion in AR, the spaceships (the right stick clicked twice), the notebook's B or Y held, and the menu, panels, cards and subtitles drawn from their first frame.
The calibration fix is untested: it rests on the bisect, not on a reproduction.
